title: Plans — round 8: your layout notes, and the Ask the assistant button

steps.headline: Approve and Comment now sit on the same line as the limit text.
steps.changed: The buttons moved up beside "5 specialists · Up to about $0.12…", using the empty space you pointed out.
steps.notice: The card is one line shorter.
steps.risk: On a narrow window the buttons drop below the text.

steps.path: Specialists popup while a plan runs next to an ordinary specialist
steps.headline: A running plan is now a "Plan: …" card the same width as the other specialists, with no separate heading.
steps.changed: The "Plans" heading is gone; the plan's card sits in the list like any specialist and opens to show its specialists.
steps.notice: Plans and ordinary specialists line up in one list.

steps.path: Below a plan card after the assistant was asked
steps.headline: The "Note for the assistant" row no longer appears in the chat.
steps.changed: The row under the card is gone, as you asked.

steps.path: A plan paused at its limit
steps.headline: A paused plan no longer hands itself to the assistant; it shows an "Ask the assistant" button instead.
steps.changed: The pause shows its reason and buttons at once. "Ask the assistant" is the light button on the left; nothing happens unless you press it.
steps.notice: No automatic messages or greyed card unless you ask.
steps.risk: You read the reason yourself first.

steps.path: After pressing Ask the assistant while it is still answering something else
steps.headline: After you ask, the card greys out and says when the assistant will look.
steps.changed: If the assistant is mid-reply the card says "The assistant will look at this after its current reply."; otherwise "The assistant is looking into this." The chat shows "You asked the assistant about this plan."
steps.notice: You know your question was received and when it will be answered.

steps.headline: If the assistant can't answer, the card says so and offers Retry.
steps.changed: The error line gives the real reason (here the provider was overloaded) with Retry, and the card's normal buttons come back.
steps.notice: A failed question never leaves the card stuck.

steps.path: A paused plan on a phone-width window
steps.headline: On a narrow window, step titles and the pause reason are readable again.
steps.changed: Titles were cut to "1." and the reason squeezed into a sliver; now titles wrap and the buttons move below the reason.
steps.notice: Plans are usable on a narrow window.
steps.risk: The card is taller on narrow windows.
